<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><a name="Item1a_RiskFactors_155417"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 1A.</font></u> &#160;<u>RISK
FACTORS</u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following is a
summary of the risk factors that we believe are most relevant to our
business.&#160; These are factors that,
individually or in the aggregate, we think could cause our actual results to
differ significantly from anticipated or historical results.&#160; You should understand that it is not possible
to predict or identify all such factors.&#160;
Consequently, you should not consider the following to be a complete
discussion of all potential risks or uncertainties.&#160; We undertake no obligation to publicly update
forward-looking statements, whether as a result of new information, future
events, or otherwise.&#160; You are advised,
however, to consult any further disclosure we make on related subjects in our
reports on forms 10-Q and 8-K filed with the SEC.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares Is
Subject To Interest Rate Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our earnings depend
largely on the relationship between the yield on our interest-earning assets
and our cost of funds. &#160;This
relationship, known as the interest rate spread, is subject to fluctuation and
is affected by economic and competitive factors which influence market interest
rates, the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing
liabilities, and the level of non-performing assets. &#160;Fluctuations in market interest rates also
affect our customers&#146; demand for our products and services.&#160; See the sections entitled &#147;Net Interest
Income and Net Interest Margin&#148; and &#147;Interest Rate Risk&#148; in Item 7 &#147;Management&#146;s
Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#148;
located elsewhere in this report for further discussion related to Bankshares&#146;
management of interest rate risk.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares Is
Subject To Lending Risk</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There are inherent risks
associated with Bankshares&#146; lending activities. &#160;These risks include, among other things, the
impact of changes in interest rates and changes in the economic conditions in
the markets in which Bankshares operates.&#160;
Increases in interest rates and/or weakening economic conditions could
adversely affect the ability of borrowers to repay outstanding loans or the
value of the collateral securing these loans. &#160;Commercial loans, including commercial real
estate loans are typically subject to a higher credit risk than other types of
loans, including residential real estate or consumer loans, because they
usually involve larger loan balances to a single borrower and are more
susceptible to a risk of default during an economic downturn.&#160; Because Bankshares&#146; loan portfolio contains a
significant number of commercial and industrial, construction and commercial
real estate loans with relatively large balances, the deterioration of one or a
few of these loans could cause a significant increase in nonperforming loans. &#160;These types of loans are also typically larger
than residential real estate loans and consumer loans.&#160;&#160; An increase in nonperforming loans could
result in a net loss of earnings from these loans, an increase in the provision
for possible loan losses and an increase in loan charge offs, all of which
could have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; financial condition and
results of operations. &#160;See the section&nbsp;captioned
&#147;Loans&#148; in Item 7. Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition
and Results of Operations located elsewhere in this report for further
discussion related to commercial and industrial, construction and commercial
real estate loans.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares&#146;
Allowance For Possible Loan Losses May&nbsp;Be Insufficient</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In an attempt to mitigate
our loan and lease losses, we maintain an allowance for loan and lease losses
based on, among other things, national and regional economic conditions,
historical loss experience and delinquency trends. &#160;However, we cannot predict loan and lease
losses with certainty, and we cannot assure you that charge-offs in future
periods will not exceed the allowance for loan and lease losses. &#160;If our allowance for loan and lease losses
were not sufficient to cover actual loan and lease losses, our earnings would
decrease.&#160; In addition, regulatory
agencies, as an integral part of their examination process, review our
allowance for loan and lease losses and may require additions to the allowance
based on their judgment about information available to them at the time of
their examination. &#160;Factors that require
an increase in our allowance for loan and lease losses could reduce our
earnings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares&#146;
Profitability Depends Significantly On Economic Conditions</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The economic impact of
the United States&#146; military operations in Iraq, as well as the war on terrorism
and the possibility of any terrorist attacks in response to these operations,
is uncertain but could have a material effect on general economic conditions,
consumer confidence and market liquidity. &#160;Further, the geographic concentration of our
business in the vicinity of the nation&#146;s capital may place our business at
greater risk of terrorist activity. &#160;A
deterioration in economic conditions in the Washington-Baltimore metropolitan
area could have a material adverse effect on the quality of our loan portfolio
and the</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">demand for our products
and services, and, accordingly, on our results of operations. &#160;No assurance can be given as to the effect of
these events on the performance of our business.&#160; Furthermore, a significant decline in general
economic conditions, caused by inflation, recession, unemployment, changes in
securities markets or other factors could impact local economic conditions and,
in turn, have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; financial condition and
results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares
Operates In A Highly Competitive Industry and Market Area</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares faces
substantial competition in all areas of its operations from a variety of
competitors, many of which are larger and may have more financial
resources.&#160; Such competitors primarily
include national, regional, and community banks within the various markets in
which Bankshares operates.&#160; Bankshares
also faces competition from many other types of financial institutions,
including, without limitation, savings and loans, credit unions, finance
companies, brokerage firms, insurance companies, factoring companies and other
financial intermediaries. &#160;The financial
services industry could become even more competitive as a result of
legislative, regulatory and technological changes and continued consolidation. &#160;Banks, securities firms and insurance
companies can merge under the umbrella of a financial holding company, which
can offer virtually any type of financial service, including banking,
securities underwriting, insurance (both agency and underwriting) and merchant
banking. &#160;Also, technology has lowered
barriers to entry and made it possible for nonbanks to offer products and services
traditionally provided by banks, such as automatic funds transfer and automatic
payment systems. &#160;Many of Bankshares&#146;
competitors have fewer regulatory constraints and may have lower cost
structures. Additionally, due to their size, many competitors may be able to
achieve economies of scale and, as a result, may offer a broader range of
products and services as well as better pricing for those products and services
than Bankshares can. Bankshares&#146; ability to compete successfully depends on a
number of factors, including, among other things:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
ability to develop, maintain and build upon long-term customer relationships
based on top quality service, high ethical standards and safe, sound assets.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
ability to expand Bankshares&#146; market position.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
scope, relevance and pricing of products and services offered to meet customer
needs and demands.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
rate at which Bankshares introduces new products and services relative to its
competitors.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Customer
satisfaction with Bankshares&#146; level of service.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Industry
and general economic trends.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Failure to perform in any
of these areas could significantly weaken Bankshares&#146; competitive position,
which could adversely affect Bankshares&#146; growth and profitability, which, in
turn, could have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; financial condition
and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares Is
Subject To Extensive Government Regulation and Supervision</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Financial institution
regulation has been the subject of significant legislation in recent years and
may be the subject of further significant legislation in the future, none of
which is within our control. &#160;Significant
new laws or changes in, or repeals of, existing laws, including with respect to
federal and state taxation, may cause our results of operations to differ
materially. &#160;Further, federal monetary
policy, particularly as implemented through the Federal Reserve, significantly
affects credit conditions for our affiliated banks, primarily through open
market operations in U.S. government securities and the discount rate for bank
borrowings and reserve requirements. &#160;A
material change in any of these conditions would have a material impact on our
results of operations.&#160; Furthermore,
failure to comply with laws, regulations or policies could result in sanctions
by regulatory agencies, civil money penalties and/or reputation damage, which
could have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; business, financial
condition and results of operations. &#160;While
Bankshares has policies and procedures designed to prevent any such violations,
there can be no assurance that such violations will not occur. See the section&nbsp;captioned
&#147;Supervision and Regulation&#148; in Item 1 &#147;Business&#148; located elsewhere in this
report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares&#146;
Controls And Procedures May&nbsp;Fail Or Be Circumvented</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management regularly
reviews and updates Bankshares&#146; internal controls, disclosure controls and
procedures, and corporate governance policies and procedures. &#160;Any system of controls, however well designed
and operated, is based in part on certain assumptions and can provide only
reasonable, not absolute, assurances that the objectives of the system will be met.
&#160;Any failure or circumvention of
Bankshares&#146; controls and procedures or failure to comply with regulations
related to controls and procedures could have a material adverse effect on
Bankshares&#146; business, results of operations and financial condition.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Potential
Acquisitions May&nbsp;Disrupt Bankshares&#146; Business And Dilute Stockholder Value</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares seeks merger
or acquisition partners that are culturally similar and have experienced
management and possess either significant market presence or have potential for
improved profitability through financial management, economies of scale or
expanded services. &#160;Acquiring other
banks, businesses, or branches involves various risks commonly associated with
acquisitions, including, among other things:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Potential
exposure to unknown or contingent liabilities of the target company.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Exposure
to potential asset quality issues of the target company.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Difficulty
and expense of integrating the operations and personnel of the target company.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Potential
disruption to Bankshares&#146; business.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Potential
diversion of Bankshares&#146; management&#146;s time and attention.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>The
possible loss of key employees and customers of the target company.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Difficulty
in estimating the value of the target company.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Potential
changes in banking or tax laws or regulations that may affect the target
company.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares regularly
evaluates merger and acquisition opportunities and conducts due diligence
activities related to possible transactions with other financial institutions
and financial services companies. &#160;As a
result, merger or acquisition discussions and, in some cases, negotiations may
take place and future mergers or acquisitions involving cash, debt or equity
securities may occur at any time. &#160;Acquisitions typically involve the payment of
a premium over book and market values and, therefore, some dilution of
Bankshares&#146; tangible book value and net income per common share may occur in
connection with any future transaction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Furthermore, failure to
realize the expected revenue increases, cost savings, increases in geographic
or product presence, and/or other projected benefits from an acquisition could
have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; financial condition and results
of operations.&#160; See Note No.&nbsp;2 &#147;Business
Combinations&#148; in the notes to consolidated financial statements included in
Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, which is located elsewhere
in this report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares May&nbsp;Not
Be Able To Attract And Retain Skilled People</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares&#146; success
depends, in large part, on its ability to attract and retain key people. &#160;Competition for the best people in the business
conducted by Bankshares can be intense and Bankshares may not be able to hire
people or to retain them. The unexpected loss of services of one or more of
Bankshares&#146; key personnel could have a material adverse impact on Bankshares&#146;
business because of their skills, knowledge of Bankshares&#146; market, years of
industry experience and the difficulty of promptly finding qualified
replacement personnel.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares&#146;
Information Systems May&nbsp;Experience An Interruption Or Breach In Security</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares relies heavily
on communications and information systems to conduct its business. &#160;Any failure, interruption or breach in
security of these systems could result in failures or disruptions in Bankshares&#146;
customer relationship management, general ledger, deposit, loan and other
systems. &#160;While Bankshares has policies
and procedures designed to prevent or limit the effect of the failure,
interruption or security breach of its information systems, there can be no
assurance that any such failures, interruptions or security breaches will not
occur or, if they do occur, that they will be adequately addressed. &#160;The occurrence of any failures, interruptions
or security breaches of Bankshares&#146; information systems could damage Bankshares&#146;
reputation, result in a loss of business, subject Bankshares to additional
regulatory scrutiny, or expose Bankshares to civil litigation and possible
financial liability, any of which could have a material adverse effect on
Bankshares&#146; financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares Continually
Encounters Technological Change</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The financial services
industry is continually undergoing rapid technological change with frequent
introductions of new technology driven products and services. &#160;The effective use of technology increases
efficiency and enables financial institutions to serve customers better and to
reduce costs. &#160;Bankshares&#146; future success
depends, in part, upon its ability to address the needs of its customers by
using technology to provide products and services that will satisfy customer
demands, as well as to create additional efficiencies in Bankshares&#146;
operations. &#160;Many of Bankshares&#146;
competitors have substantially greater resources to invest in technological
improvements. &#160;Bankshares may not be able
to effectively implement new technology driven products and services or be
successful in marketing these products and services to its customers. &#160;Failure to keep pace successfully with
technological change affecting the financial services industry could have a
material adverse impact on Bankshares&#146; business and, in turn, Bankshares&#146;
financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares Is
Subject To Claims and Litigation Pertaining To Fiduciary Responsibility</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">From time to time, customers
make claims and take legal action pertaining to Bankshares&#146; performance of its
fiduciary responsibilities. &#160;Whether
customer claims and legal action related to Bankshares&#146; performance of its
fiduciary responsibilities are founded or unfounded, if such claims and legal
actions are not resolved in a manner favorable to Bankshares they may result in
significant financial liability and/or adversely affect the market perception
of Bankshares and its products and services as well as affect customer demand
for those products and services. &#160;Any
financial liability or reputation damage could have a material adverse effect
on Bankshares&#146; business, which, in turn, could have a material adverse effect
on Bankshares&#146; financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Severe Weather,
Natural Disasters, Acts Of War Or Terrorism And Other External Events Could
Significantly Impact Bankshares&#146; Business</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Severe weather, natural
disasters, acts of war or terrorism and other adverse external events could
have a significant impact on Bankshares&#146; ability to conduct business. &#160;Such events could affect the stability of
Bankshares&#146; deposit base, impair the ability of borrowers to repay outstanding
loans, impair the value of collateral securing loans, cause significant
property damage, result in loss of revenue and/or cause Bankshares to incur
additional expenses.&#160; Although management
has established disaster recovery policies and procedures, the occurrence of
any such event could have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; business,
which, in turn, could have a material adverse effect on Bankshares&#146; financial
condition and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Bankshares
Relies On Dividends From Its Subsidiaries For Most Of Its Revenue</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are a financial
holding company and a bank holding company and as a result, much of our income consists
of dividends received from our affiliated banks. &#160;This means we rely primarily upon dividends
from our affiliated banks to pay dividends to Bankshares&#146; common
stockholders.&#160; Federal and state bank
regulations restrict the amounts when our affiliated banks pay dividends
directly or indirectly to us, when making any extensions of credit to us, when
transferring assets to us and when investing in our stock or securities. &#160;These regulations also prevent us from borrowing
from our affiliated banks unless the loans are secured by collateral. &#160;In addition, we cannot assure that our
affiliated banks will be able to continue to pay dividends to us at past
levels, if at all. &#160;If we do not receive
sufficient cash dividends or borrowings from our affiliate banks, we may not
have sufficient funds to pay dividends on common stock.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="font-size:10.0pt;line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><a name="Item1b_UnresolvedStaffComments_155424"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 1B.</font></u>&#160; <u>UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS</u></p>

<p align="left" style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="left" style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">There were no unresolved staff comments as of December&nbsp;31,
2005.</font></p>

<p align="left" style="line-height:normal;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><a name="Item2_Properties_155432"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 2.</font></u>&#160; <u>PROPERTIES</u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
main offices of Bankshares and MSD&amp;T are located in a 21-story building at
Two Hopkins Plaza in Baltimore, Maryland, which is owned by MBC Realty, LLC, a
wholly owned subsidiary of Harbor Group International, L.L.C.&#160; Pursuant to a lease agreement by and between
MBC Realty, LLC (which was previously owned by Bankshares) and MSD&amp;T,
effective as of December&nbsp;13, 2004, MSD&amp;T agreed to lease up to
approximately 179,000 square feet of prime office space and approximately
27,000 square feet&nbsp;of<br>
back-office&nbsp;and storage space at Two Hopkins Plaza, for a term of ten
years.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2005,
MSD&amp;T and Bankshares occupied approximately 206,000 square feet. &#160;The lease agreement contains two five-year
renewal options. &#160;The lease agreement
requires aggregate annual rent of approximately $3.9 million in 2005.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2005, Bankshares also
occupied approximately 132,000 square feet of leased space in a building
located in Linthicum, Maryland, in which its operations and certain other
departments are located, and a 7,000 square foot call center facility in
Federalsburg, Maryland.&#160; The Linthicum
and Federalsburg properties are owned by Bankshares. &#160;Of the 240 banking offices, 112 are owned in
fee, 33 are owned subject to ground leases and 95 are leased, with aggregate
annual rentals, not including the branch located at Two Hopkins Plaza, of
approximately $10.6 million as of December&nbsp;31, 2005.</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_155438"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 3.</font></u>&#160; <u>LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Between 2001 and 2003, on
behalf of either individual plaintiffs or a putative class of plaintiffs, eight
separate actions were filed in state and federal court against Community Bank
of Northern Virginia (&#147;CBNV&#148;) and other defendants challenging the validity of
second mortgage loans the defendants made to the plaintiffs.&#160; All of the cases were either filed in or
removed to the federal district court for the Western District of
Pennsylvania.&#160; In June&nbsp;2003, the
parties to the various actions informed the court that they had reached an
agreement in principle to settle the various actions.&#160; On July&nbsp;17, 2003, the court conditionally
certified a class for settlement purposes, preliminarily approved the class
settlement, and directed the issuance of notice to the class.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Thereafter, certain
plaintiffs who had initially opted out of the proposed settlement and other
objectors challenged the validity of the settlement in the district court.&#160; The district court denied their arguments and
approved the settlement.&#160; These &#147;opt out&#148;
plaintiffs and other objectors appealed the district court&#146;s approval of the
settlement to the Third Circuit Court of Appeals.&#160; In August&nbsp;2005, the Third Circuit
reversed the district court&#146;s approval of the settlement and remanded the case
to the district court with instructions to consider and address certain
specific issues when re-evaluating the settlement. Certain individuals who were
excluded from the settlement class have filed two actions on behalf of a
putative class of plaintiffs alleging claims similar to those raised in the
initial filing.&#160; These actions recently
were consolidated in the Western District of Pennsylvania.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><a name="Item4_SubmissionOfMattersToAVoteO_155444"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ITEM 4.</font></u>&#160; <u>SUBMISSION OF MATTERS TO A VOTE OF SECURITY
HOLDERS</u></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="color:blue;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">No
matter was submitted during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year covered by
this Report to a vote of security holders, which is required to be disclosed
pursuant to the instructions contained in the form for this Report.</font></p>

<p style="color:blue;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" color="black" face="Times New Roman" style="color:windowtext;font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No family relationships,
as defined by the rules&nbsp;and regulations of the Securities and Exchange
Commission, exist</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">among any of the
Executive Officers. All officers are elected annually by the Board of Directors
and hold office at the pleasure of the Board. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective March&nbsp;1,
2001, Mr.&nbsp;Kelly became President and Chief Executive of Bankshares and
Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer of MSD&amp;T.&#160; In addition, effective March&nbsp;1, 2003 Mr.&nbsp;Kelly
became Chairman of Bankshares. Mr.&nbsp;Kelly served as Managing Director, Head
of Global Financial Institutions, and as Co-Head of Investment Banking Client
Management of J. P. Morgan, Chase&nbsp;&amp; Co. during January&nbsp;2001.&#160; Prior thereto, he was a Managing Director of J.
P. Morgan&nbsp;&amp; Co. Incorporated and held the following additional
positions with that Company: Head, Global Financial Institutions from February,
2000 through December, 2000; Co-Head, Global Financial Institutions and Head,
Latin America Investment Banking from December&nbsp;1997 through February&nbsp;2000;
Member, Global Investment Banking Committee from December&nbsp;1997 through December&nbsp;2000;
and Co-Head, Financial Institutions (Americas) from February&nbsp;1996 through December&nbsp;1997.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Mason joined
Bankshares in November&nbsp;2003, and is Vice Chairman of Bankshares.&#160; Effective January&nbsp;2, 2004, he was named
Bankshares&#146; Chief Operating Officer. Prior to joining Bankshares, he was Vice
Chairman of Deutsche Bank in the Americas and Managing Director of Deutsche
Bank Securities.&#160; He also served as chief
operating officer of the firm&#146;s Global Corporate Finance Department and headed
up the firm&#146;s Global Industry Group practice.&#160;
He was elected a director of MSD&amp;T in January&nbsp;2005, and a
director of Bankshares in January&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Wilson has been
a Vice Chairman of Bankshares and Chief Executive Officer of the Investment and
Wealth Management Division of MSD&amp;T since January&nbsp;2005.&#160; From September&nbsp;1998 until December&nbsp;2004,
he was General Partner of Spring Capital Partners, L.P., a private equity fund
providing expansion and acquisition capital to emerging growth companies. He
was elected a director of MSD&amp;T in January&nbsp;2005, and a director of
Bankshares in January&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Reid was elected
President and Chief Operating Officer of MSD&amp;T in September&nbsp;1997. He
joined MSD&amp;T as a Senior Vice President in 1993 and served as an Executive
Vice President from 1994 until September&nbsp;1997.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Floeckher was
appointed Executive Vice President and Head of the Affiliates for Bankshares in
November&nbsp;2003.&#160; He served as President
and Chief Executive Officer of Citizens National Bank from 1995 until November&nbsp;2003.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Floeckher is
responsible for oversight of the Banks, which includes risk management,
compliance and enhanced performance through coordinated sharing of best practices.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Troupe has been
Chief Financial Officer of Bankshares and MSD&amp;T since he joined the Bank in
September&nbsp;1996.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Unger became
General Counsel on March&nbsp;23, 2002 and was elected Secretary of Bankshares
and MSD&amp;T on July&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2002.&#160;
Prior to joining Bankshares, Mr.&nbsp;Unger was General Counsel to IMI
Resort Holdings,&nbsp;Inc., a privately held real estate company in Greenville,
South Carolina.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Paese was named
Chief Administrative Officer of Bankshares in November&nbsp;2004 and became
Chief Risk Officer on January&nbsp;2, 2005.&#160;
He joined MSD&amp;T as a Senior Vice President and Deputy General
Counsel in January&nbsp;2003.&#160; Before
joining Mercantile, Mr.&nbsp;Paese was Senior Counsel to the Financial Services
Committee of the U.S. House of Representatives (minority).&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Paese advised the Committee on legal
and policy issues relating to U.S. capital markets and corporate
governance.&#160; Prior thereto, Mr.&nbsp;Paese
was a Vice President in equity capital markets, at J .P. Morgan&nbsp;&amp; Co.
Incorporated.&#160; Prior thereto, Mr.&nbsp;Paese
was an associate at Davis Polk&nbsp;&amp; Wardwell.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mrs.&nbsp;Kakaris has
been an Executive Vice President of Bankshares and MSD&amp;T since 2002.&#160; She is responsible for Operations and
Technology Services.&#160; Mrs.&nbsp;Kakaris
joined the bank in 1988 and served as a Senior Vice President from 1997 until March&nbsp;2002.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ms.&nbsp;Simmons joined
Bankshares in 2003, after the merger with F&amp;M Bancorp.&#160; She had been Treasurer of F&amp;M Bancorp
since 2000 and Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of Farmers&nbsp;&amp;
Mechanics Bank since 2000. Prior to that time, Ms.&nbsp;Simmons served as
Senior Vice President of Finance and Treasurer of Citizens Bancorp from 1989 to
1997.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mr.&nbsp;Skinner has been
Senior Vice President and Controller of Bankshares since 1998.&#160; He served as Controller of MSD&amp;T since
1996.&#160; Mr.&nbsp;Skinner joined MSD&amp;T
in 1979.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_155509"></a><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">Item
7.</font></u><font style="text-transform:uppercase;">&#160; <u>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of
Financial Condition and Results of Operations</u></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">I. EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mercantile Bankshares
Corporation (&#147;Bankshares&#148;) is a regional multibank holding company
headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland.&#160; At
December&nbsp;31, 2005, Bankshares had $16.4 billion in assets, $11.6 billion
in loans and $12.1 billion in deposits.&#160;
It is the largest bank holding company headquartered in the state of
Maryland.&#160; The two principal lines of
business are Banking and Investment&nbsp;&amp; Wealth Management (&#147;IWM&#148;),
delivered through the lead bank Mercantile-Safe Deposit and Trust Company (&#147;MSD&amp;T&#148;)
and 10 affiliated banks.&#160; See &#147;Segment
Reporting&#148; in section&nbsp;&#147;II. </font>ANALYSIS OF OPERATING RESULTS FOR 2005 TO 2004&#148; for more
information.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January 10, 2006,
Bankshares announced a three-for-two stock split on its common stock, payable
in the form of a stock dividend on January 27, 2006 to stockholders of record
as of the close of business on January 20, 2006. &#160;Certain shares, average shares and per share
amounts have been adjusted to give effect to the split.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares recorded its 30<sup>th</sup>
consecutive year of increased net income in 2005.&#160; Net income for Bankshares was $276.3 million
for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, compared with $229.4 million for the
year 2004, representing a 20.4% increase.&#160;
Diluted net income per common share for 2005 increased by 17.7% to $2.26
compared with $1.92 for 2004.&#160; The most
noteworthy factors affecting 2005 earnings were the acquisition of Community
Bank of Northern Virginia (&#147;CBNV&#148;), improvement in the net interest margin,
growth in loans and improving credit quality.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On May&nbsp;18, 2005,
Bankshares completed its acquisition of CBNV, a bank headquartered in Sterling,
Virginia, which was merged into MSD&amp;T.&#160;
CBNV operated 14 branch offices in the Northern Virginia metropolitan
market at the time of the acquisition.&#160; The
consideration paid to CBNV shareholders in connection with the acquisition was
comprised of $82.9 million in cash and 3.7 million shares of Bankshares&#146; common
stock as adjusted to give effect to the stock split.&#160; CBNV transactions have been included in
Bankshares&#146; financial results subsequent to May&nbsp;18, 2005.&#160; The assets and liabilities of CBNV were
recorded on the Consolidated Balance Sheet at their respective fair
values.&#160; The fair values were determined
as of May&nbsp;18, 2005, and are subject to refinement as further information
becomes available.&#160; The transaction
resulted in total assets acquired as of May&nbsp;18, 2005 of $888.2 million,
including $671.0 million of loans and leases; liabilities assumed were $842.3
million, including $626.9 million of deposits.&#160;
Bankshares recorded $162.1 million of goodwill and $4.6 million of core
deposit intangible (&#147;CDI&#148;).&#160; CDI is
subject to amortization and is being amortized over nine years on a
straight-line basis.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Governors of
the Federal Reserve System (&#147;Federal Reserve Board&#148;) increased short-term rates
by 125 basis points in 2004 and 200 basis points in 2005.&#160; The net interest margin improved 9 basis
points to 4.44% for 2005 from 4.35% for 2004, which compares favorably with the
increase of 3 basis points experienced during 2004.&#160; The net interest margin for 2003 was
4.32%.&#160; The 2005 net interest margin
increase was attributable to a 20 basis point increase in the benefit derived
from noninterest-bearing sources of funds, which was partially offset by an 11
basis point decline in the spread between the yield on earning assets and the
cost of interest-bearing liabilities.&#160;
Competition to gather deposits increased throughout the year and
resulted in higher rates paid on these funds.&#160;
See &#147;Analysis of Interest Rate and Interest Differentials&#148; and the
discussions of &#147;Net Interest Income&#148; and &#147;Interest Rate Risk&#148; found in Item 7
of this report.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31,
2005, loans outstanding were $11.6 billion, an increase of 13.5% over the $10.2
billion outstanding at December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2004.&#160; Much of the lending growth was driven by
strong real estate markets for both commercial and residential properties.&#160; Construction loans at December&nbsp;31, 2005
were $1.6 billion, an increase of 26.7% from $1.3 billion at December&nbsp;31,
2004.&#160; Commercial real estate loans were
$3.7 billion at December&nbsp;31, 2005, an increase of 18.6% from $3.1 billion
at December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; Commercial
and industrial loans grew by 3.2%.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Credit quality measures
improved on both an absolute and relative basis.&#160; Nonperforming loans declined from $30.9
million at December&nbsp;31, 2004 to $22.6 million at December&nbsp;31,
2005.&#160; This is the lowest level reported
at year-end since December&nbsp;31, 1999.&#160;
Nonperforming loans as a percent of year-end loans were 0.19% at December&nbsp;31,
2005.&#160; On a relative basis, this is their
lowest level at year-end in more than 20 years.&#160;
Reflecting these improvements, the provision for loan losses declined by
$5.6 million to $1.6 million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,&nbsp;2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2005 Bankshares
experienced improvements in return on average assets (&#147;ROA&#148;) and return on
average shareholders&#146; equity (&#147;ROE&#148;). The 2005 ROA increased to 1.78% from
1.64% in 2004. Bankshares&#146; 2005 ROE increased to 13.18% from 12.26% in
2004.&#160; Average shareholders&#146; equity to
average assets was at 13.51% for 2005, an increase from 13.38% for 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares
also reports cash operating earnings, defined as </font>&#147;GAAP&#148;
(Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) earnings excluding the amortization
of intangible assets associated with purchase accounting for business
combinations; securities gains and losses; and other significant gains, losses
or expenses (such as those associated with integrating acquired entities&#146;
operations into Bankshares) unrelated to
Bankshares&#146; core operations.&#160; We believe these non-GAAP measures
provide information useful to investors in understanding our ongoing core
business and operational performance trends.&#160;
These measures should not be viewed as a substitute for GAAP.&#160; Management believes presentations of
financial measures excluding the impact of certain items provide useful
supplemental</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">information and better
reflect its core operating activities.&#160;
In order to arrive at core business operating results, the effects of
certain noncore business transactions, such as gains and losses on the sales of
securities, amortization of intangibles, restructuring charges and
merger-related expenses, have been excluded.&#160;
Management reviews these same measures internally.&#160; For instance, the cash operating efficiency
ratio, rather than the GAAP basis efficiency ratio, is used to measure
management&#146;s success at controlling ongoing, core operating expenses.&#160; We believe these measures are consistent with
how investors and analysts typically evaluate our industry, and by providing
these measures, we facilitate their analysis.&#160;
Cash operating earnings totaled
$279.6 million for 2005, an increase of 18.7% over $235.5 million
for&nbsp;2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additionally, management
believes that reporting several key measures based on tangible assets (total
assets less intangible assets) and tangible equity (total equity less
intangible assets) is important, as this more closely approximates the basis
for measuring the adequacy of capital for regulatory purposes.&#160; For the year 2005, the return on average
tangible assets was 1.89% compared with 1.75% for 2004.&#160; The ratio of average tangible equity to
average tangible assets was 9.70% for 2005 and 2004.&#160; See &#147;Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures&#148; for
the reconciliation of GAAP measures to non-GAAP measures in the section&nbsp;captioned
&#147;II. ANALYSIS OF OPERATING RESULTS FOR 2005 TO 2004&#148; elsewhere in Item 7.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The remaining sections of
Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations will provide a more detailed explanation of the important trends and
material changes in components of our consolidated financial statements.&#160; The discussion suggests that sustaining
future earnings growth comparable to our experience in past years will require,
among other things, efficient generation of loan growth in a competitive
market, while maintaining an adequate spread between yields on earning assets
and the cost of funds.&#160; Our degree of
success in meeting these goals depends on unpredictable factors such as
possible changes in prevailing interest rates, the mix of deposits, credit
quality and general economic conditions.&#160;
This discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the
consolidated financial statements and other financial information presented in
this Report.</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies and
Related Estimates</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Set forth below is a
discussion of the accounting policies and related estimates that management
believes are the most critical to understanding Bankshares&#146; consolidated
financial statements, financial condition and results of operations, and which
require complex management judgments, uncertainties and/or estimates.&#160; Information regarding Bankshares&#146; other
accounting policies is included in Note No.&nbsp;1 (Significant Accounting
Policies) of the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Investment Securities</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment securities
classified as &#147;held-to-maturity&#148; are acquired with the intent and ability to
hold until maturity and are carried at cost.&#160;
Investment securities classified as &#147;available-for-sale&#148; are acquired to
be held for indefinite periods and may be sold in response to changes in
interest rates and/or prepayment risk or for liquidity management
purposes.&#160; These securities are carried
at fair value.&#160; Securities may become
impaired on an other-than-temporary basis, which involves a degree of
judgment.&#160; Therefore, an assessment is
made at the end of each quarter to determine whether there have been any events
or economic circumstances to indicate that a security is impaired on an
other-than-temporary basis.&#160; An
other-than-temporary impairment may develop if, based on all available
evidence, the carrying amount of the investment is not recoverable within a
reasonable period.&#160; Factors considered in
making this assessment include among others, the intent and ability to hold the
investment for a period sufficient for a recovery in value, external credit
ratings and recent downgrades, market price fluctuations due to factors other
than interest rates, and the probability of collection of contractual cash
flows.&#160; Securities on which there is an
unrealized loss deemed to be other-than-temporary are written down to fair
value, and the adjustment is recorded as a realized loss.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Arriving at an appropriate
level of allowance for loan losses involves a high degree of judgment.
Bankshares&#146; allowance for loan losses provides for probable losses based on
evaluations of known and inherent risks in the loan portfolio.&#160; Management uses historical quantitative information
to assess the adequacy of the allowance for loan losses as well as qualitative
information about the prevailing economic and business environment among other
things.&#160; The allowance for loan losses is
comprised of specific allocations to impaired loans and general allocations to
pools of loans not deemed impaired that include an unallocated amount.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The specific allowance
allocation is based on an analysis of the loan portfolio.&#160; Each loan with an outstanding balance in
excess of a specified threshold that is either in nonaccrual status or on the Watchlist
is evaluated.&#160; The Watchlist represents
loans identified and closely followed by management.&#160; They possess certain qualities or
characteristics that may lead to collection and loss issues.&#160; The identified loans are evaluated for
potential loss in accordance with Statement of Financial Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;)
No.&nbsp;114, &#147;Accounting for Creditors for Impairment of a Loan&#148; and SFAS No.&nbsp;118,
&#147;Accounting for Creditors for Impairment of a Loan &#150; Income Recognition and
Disclosure&#148; by analyzing current collateral values or present value of cash
flows, as well as the capacity of the guarantor, as applicable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The general allowance
calculation begins with segmentation of the remaining (unimpaired) portfolio
according to loan types. Historical loss factors are maintained for each loan
type, providing the starting point of the analysis.&#160; Historical loss factors are applied to all
non-Watchlist loans.&#160; Management is
currently utilizing the past five-year loss history specific to each major
segment to perform the allocation.&#160;
Historical loss factors are adjusted to reflect the point in time that
management initially identified a potential impairment loss in such risk-rated
loans as opposed to when such loss is actually taken as a charge-off against
the allowance.&#160; This adjustment is
necessary, as Bankshares&#146; practice has generally been to work with its
borrowers through their economic difficulties and record a charge-off when all
recovery efforts have been exhausted.&#160;
Accordingly, historical losses may tend to lag the national and regional
economic cycles.&#160; Bankshares also has
developed data on probability of default and loss given default, which have
been incorporated for the higher risk rated credits, which include Watchlist
loans that are not currently impaired.&#160;
Those loss factors are then applied to all loans within the same risk
rating.&#160; Qualitative factors that may
cause credit losses to deviate from average historical experience are then
developed.&#160; These include, but are not
limited to: changes in the volume and severity of past due loans; changes in
the volume of Watchlist loans and nonaccruals; concentrations in a specific
industry or geographic location; administrative risk concerns that include
changes in the loan review and loan grading system; changes in lending policies
and procedures (which include underwriting, collection, charge-off and recovery
practices); changes in management or the staff of any previously mentioned
areas; and current economic conditions and indicators.&#160; Both internal and external peer data are
utilized as applicable to establish these factors.&#160; Management&#146;s judgment and experience are key
to this process.&#160; These factors are
revised to address current conditions and trends in the portfolio.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The allowance amount not
allocated represents the differential between the combined specific and general
allocations and the actual allowance recorded on the books.&#160; The unallocated allowance recognizes the
imprecision inherent in estimating and measuring loss when allocating the
allowance to individual, or pools of, loans.&#160;
It also takes into consideration the allowance level deemed appropriate
by each affiliate based on its local knowledge and input from bank regulators
and their view from the standpoint of safety and soundness, among other
factors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For a full discussion of
Bankshares&#146; methodology for assessing the adequacy of the allowance for loan
losses, see &#147;Allowance for Loan Losses&#148; found elsewhere in Item 7 and Note No.&nbsp;1
(Significant Accounting Policies) of the financial statements.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">23</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans in Nonaccrual
Status or Deemed to Be Impaired</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A loan asset will be classified and placed
into nonaccrual status when the principal or interest payments on any loan
(e.g., commercial, mortgage and construction loans) are past due 90 days or
more at the end of a calendar quarter or the payment in full of principal or
interest is not expected.&#160; Any accrued
but uncollected interest is reversed at that time.&#160; Consumer installment loans are charged off
when they become 90 days past due at the end of the quarter.&#160; Additionally, a loan may be put on nonaccrual
status sooner than 90 days, if in management&#146;s judgment, the loan or portion
thereof is deemed uncollectible.&#160;
Bankshares ceases to accrue interest income on such loans. Subsequent
receipts on nonaccrual loans are recorded as a reduction of principal, and
interest income is recorded only once principal recovery is reasonably
assured.&#160; Generally, a loan may be
restored to accrual status when all past due principal, interest and late
charges have been paid and the Bank expects repayment of the remaining
contractual principal and interest.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A loan is considered impaired, based on current information and events,
if it is probable that Bankshares will not collect all principal and interest
payments according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160; Impaired loans do not include large groups of
smaller balance homogeneous loans that are evaluated collectively for
impairment (e.g., residential mortgages and consumer installment loans).&#160; The impairment of a loan is measured based on
the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#146;s
effective interest rate, or the fair value of the collateral if the repayment
is expected to be provided predominantly by the underlying collateral.&#160; A majority of Bankshares&#146; impaired loans are
measured by reference to the fair value of the collateral.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares recognizes deferred
income tax assets and liabilities for the future tax effects of temporary
differences, net operating loss carryovers and tax credits.&#160; Deferred tax assets are subject to
management&#146;s judgment, based on available evidence, that future realization is
more likely than not.&#160; If management determines
that Bankshares may be unable to realize all or part of net deferred tax assets
in the future, then Bankshares would be required to record a valuation
allowance against such deferred tax asset.&#160;
In such an event, a direct charge to income tax expense may be required
to reduce the recorded value of the net deferred tax asset to the expected
realizable amount.&#160; For more information
regarding Bankshares&#146; accounting for income taxes, see Note No. 12 (Income
Taxes) of the financial statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Valuation of Goodwill/Intangible Assets and
Analysis for Impairment </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares has increased its market share, in part, through the
acquisition of entire financial institutions accounted for under the purchase
method of accounting, as well as from the purchase of other financial
institutions&#146; branches (not the entire institution). Bankshares is required to
record assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their fair value, which
involves an estimate determined by the use of internal or other valuation
techniques.&#160; See Note No.&nbsp;19
(Goodwill and Intangible Assets) of the financial statements for further
information on the accounting for goodwill and other intangible assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">II. ANALYSIS OF OPERATING RESULTS FOR 2005 TO 2004</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Segment Reporting</font></b></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares reports two distinct business segments, Banking and
Investment&nbsp;&amp; Wealth Management, for which financial information is
segregated for use in assessing performance and allocating resources when
reporting to the Board of Directors.&#160; The
Banking segment consists of the group of 11 affiliate banks and mortgage-banking
activities.&#160; A schedule&nbsp;disclosing
the details of these operating segments can be found in Note No.&nbsp;16
(Segment Reporting) of the financial statements.&#160; Segment financial information is subjective
and, unlike financial accounting, is not necessarily based on GAAP.&#160; As a result, financial information of the
reporting segments is not necessarily comparable with similar information
reported by others and may not be comparable with Bankshares&#146; consolidated
results.&#160; Certain expense amounts, such
as operations overhead, have been reclassified from internal financial
reporting in order to provide for proper allocation of costs in the reported
data.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the fourth quarter of 2005, the Private Banking Group of MSD&amp;T
was consolidated into the Private Banking Group of IWM.&#160; The segment results have been reclassified to
conform to current presentation for comparability.&#160; Additionally, as loans and deposits are now
being reflected in the IWM segment, a funds transfer-pricing model was utilized
to match the duration of the funding and investment of the IWM segment&#146;s assets
and liabilities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">24</font></p>
