<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Banking</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Banking segment includes the Retail, Small Business, Commercial and
Mortgage Banking lines of business.&#160;
Banking products include:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Retail Banking</font></i>:&#160;
Checking, savings and money market accounts, time deposits and IRAs,
insurance, equity lines and loans, lines of credit, and equipment and
transportation (auto, recreational vehicle and marine) loans.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Small Business Banking</font></i>:&#160;
Deposit and credit products and services to businesses with annual
revenues up to $3.0 million or credit needs up to $750.0 thousand, including
receivables and inventory financing, equipment leases, and real estate
financing.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Commercial Banking</font></i>:&#160;
Commercial deposit, lending and commercial real estate solutions to
businesses typically with annual revenues between $4.0 million and $50.0
million, and including commercial loans and lines of credit, letters of credit,
asset-based lending, commercial real estate, construction loans, capital market
products and insurance.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Mortgage Banking</font></i>:&#160;
Commercial, multi-family and residential mortgage loan origination and
servicing.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:none;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <td width="13" style="border:none;"></td>
  <td width="10" style="border:none;"></td>
  <td width="71" style="border:none;"></td>
  <td width="6" style="border:none;"></td>
 </tr>
</table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the second quarter of 2005, Bankshares consolidated Fidelity Bank
into Farmers&nbsp;&amp; Mechanics Bank.&#160;
The consolidation of these banks enables the surviving bank, Farmers&nbsp;&amp;
Mechanics, to serve its local customers with greater size and expertise.&#160; Also in the second quarter of 2005,
Mercantile Potomac Bank merged into MSD&amp;T.&#160;
This combination allows Bankshares to provide the capital resources
necessary for expansion into the Washington, D.C. and Northern Virginia
markets.&#160; Further, the merger of CBNV
into the Mercantile Potomac Division of MSD&amp;T was completed in the second
quarter.&#160; Mercantile Potomac Bank and
Fidelity Bank will continue to serve their respective markets under their own
names with local leadership and decision-making.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the third quarter of 2004, Bankshares consolidated 11 affiliate
banks into four banks.&#160; The consolidated
banks shared common markets.&#160; The
consolidation of these banks enables the surviving banks to serve their local
customers with greater size, scale and expertise.&#160; This initiative was not undertaken to reduce
operating costs, although some savings arose out of the consolidation.&#160; The initiative was undertaken to enable these
banks to streamline operating processes, controls and compliance efforts; recruit
seasoned professionals to these markets; and provide a greater breadth of
services at the local level.&#160; Bankshares
is committed to the affiliate bank model, whereby local boards of directors
provide strong oversight, and bank presidents maintain strong relationships
within the community. In 2004, Banking incurred approximately $3.6 million in
restructuring charges related to the consolidations. A majority of these costs
was in severance charges and other personnel costs of approximately $2.3
million, with $1.1 million in legal and consulting fees.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Banking segment, which contributed 86.0% of total revenue,
continued to experience strong loan and deposit growth.&#160; The Banking segment was the primary
beneficiary of the CBNV acquisition.&#160; The
addition of CBNV during 2005 had an impact on nearly every line of the
consolidated balance sheet and statement of consolidated income, as well as the
performance of the Banking segment, as set forth below.&#160; Net income for Banking for 2005 increased
22.9% to $271.4 million from $220.9 million for 2004.&#160; The Banking segment&#146;s operating leverage
improved over the comparative period, with revenue growth of 15.4% and expense growth
of 7.8%, which includes the addition of CBNV. Net interest income for Banking
increased 14.1% to $609.8 million for 2005 from $534.5 million for 2004. The
growth in net interest income in 2005 was largely attributable to a 13.4%
increase in average loans outstanding, with the CBNV acquisition contributing
approximately 32.1% of this growth.&#160; See the
analysis of net interest income included in the section&nbsp;captioned &#147;Net
Interest Income and Net Interest Margin&#148; included elsewhere in this document.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">25</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a reflection of the overall improvement in the Banking credit
quality trends, Banking recorded a decrease of $5.6 million in the provision
for loan losses for 2005.&#160; Banking
recorded a provision for loan losses of $1.6 million in 2005 compared with $7.2
million in 2004.&#160; The allowance as a
percentage of loans was 1.35% at year-end 2005 compared with 1.46% at year-end
2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average loans outstanding increased 13.6% to $10.9 billion for
2005.&#160; Commercial loans excluding the
leasing portfolio (which is in the process of paying down as Bankshares has
reduced the scope of this business) increased 5.0%, while commercial real
estate increased 19.0% from the 2004 average.&#160;
Construction loans increased 28.7%, while consumer loans increased
13.0%, from 2004 levels.&#160; Residential
real estate loans increased 9.1% from 2004. &#160;The CBNV acquisition contributed approximately
32.1% of the average loan growth in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average deposits for Banking increased 10.9% to $11.4 billion in
2005.&#160; All deposit categories increased
from the 2004 average outstandings.&#160; The
strongest year-over-year growth was in certificates of deposit,
noninterest-bearing deposits and money market deposit accounts with growth
percentages of 19.9%, 9.3% and 8.5%, respectively.&#160; The CBNV acquisition contributed
approximately 34.8% of this deposit growth.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The year-over-year increases in noninterest income and noninterest
expenses from 2004 are primarily attributable to the CBNV acquisition,
increased deposit activities and branch expansion.&#160; Noninterest income increased by $17.7 million
in 2005, with gains on sales of bank premises increasing $2.7 million, mortgage
banking fees increasing $3.5 million, nonmarketable investments increasing $2.6
million, insurance fees increasing $1.8 million and electronic banking fees
increasing $2.2 million.&#160; These gains
were partially offset by a decrease of $0.6 million in deposit service
charges.&#160; Noninterest expenses increased
by $22.8 million from 2004.&#160; This
increase was partially attributable to the $8.2 million in additional operating
expenses related to the CBNV acquisition.&#160;
More than 41.0% of the increase in total noninterest expense is related
to salaries and benefits, which grew by $11.2 million.&#160; Incentive compensation linked to improved
operating performance increased $7.7 million and pension expense increased $1.3
million.&#160; Occupancy expense increased by
$3.6 million and electronic banking costs increased by $2.4&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Investment&nbsp;&amp; Wealth Management</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IWM
includes Retail Brokerage Services, Private Wealth Management, Institutional
Investment Management, Private Banking and Mercantile Funds.&#160; IWM provides a full line of investment
products and retirement, tax and estate planning services. IWM products
include:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Retail Brokerage Services</font></i>: Stocks, bonds, proprietary and
nonproprietary mutual funds, fixed and variable annuities.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Private Wealth Management Services</font></i>: Proprietary and
nonproprietary mutual funds, proprietary and nonproprietary separate account
management, customized wealth advisory services, defined benefit and defined
contribution retirement services, family office services, individual and
institutional trust services and custody services.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Institutional Investment Management</font></i>:&#160; Sophisticated investment management and
administrative services for employee retirement plans, profit-sharing plans and
endowments.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Private Banking Services</font></i>: Deposits, loans, and mortgages.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="3" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#149;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i><font style="font-style:italic;">Mercantile Funds</font></i>:&#160;
Proprietary stock, taxable and nontaxable fixed income, money market
mutual funds and registered hedge funds of funds.</p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-autospace:ideograph-numeric ideograph-other;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the fourth quarter of 2005, the Private Banking Group of MSD&amp;T
was consolidated into the Private Banking Group of IWM.&#160; The segment results have been reclassified to
conform to current presentation for comparability.&#160; Additionally, as loans and deposits are now
being reflected in the IWM segment, a funds transfer-pricing model was utilized
to match the duration of the funding and investment of the IWM&#146;s segment assets
and liabilities.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">26</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left"></div>

</div>
<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='26',FILE='C:\JMS\sethu\06-1934-1\task911748\1934-1-ba-03.htm',USER='sesankaran',CD='Mar 13 22:26 2006' -->


<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Ongoing
progress was made in expanding the IWM business and upgrading client services.&#160; Resources related to new business development
and client service were added.&#160; Product
breadth was enhanced with the expansion of the open architecture platform that
provides clients with access to a selected group of external separate account
managers and mutual funds to complement Bankshares&#146; proprietary products.&#160; Resources were also added in the DC/Virginia
market, and Bankshares&#146; acquisition of CBNV has provided a larger distribution
network in Northern Virginia.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net
income in IWM decreased slightly to $16.2 million in 2005, from $16.5 million
in 2004 primarily due to a reduction in net interest income in the Private
Banking Group.&#160; Net interest income
declined due to lower earnings attributed to noninterest-bearing demand deposit
accounts due to greater volatility in customer balances during 2005.&#160; Excluding the Private Banking Group, IWM net
income increased $1.3 million, or 11.5%, from the previous year.&#160; Pretax profit margins, prior to corporate
overhead allocation, were 29.9% and 31.1% for 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The rise in equity markets immediately following the November&nbsp;2004
election was sustained through most of 2005.&#160;
While the S&amp;P&nbsp;500 ended 2005 only 2.8% ahead of December&nbsp;2004,
most months during the year were 4.0% to 6.0% ahead of the comparable month in
2004.&#160; Other major indices had mixed
results.&#160; Between December&nbsp;31, 2004
and December&nbsp;31, 2005, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.6% and
the Nasdaq was up 1.4%.&#160; In fixed income
markets, the Lehman Aggregate Bond Index was down 2.5% for the year.&#160; Given the relatively balanced weighting of
equities and fixed income within Bankshares&#146; investment asset base, the markets
overall provided a modest boost in 2005.&#160;
As of December&nbsp;31, 2005, 44% of IWM&#146;s managed assets were invested
in equities, including real estate.&#160;
Approximately 38% of IWM&#146;s managed assets were invested in fixed income
securities and 18% were invested in cash and other.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <td width="12%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.0%;">
  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">106.0</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
 <tr>
  <td width="57%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:57.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Year-over-Year % Change</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
  </td>
  <td width="12%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.0%;">
  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">-2.5</font></b></p>
  </td>
  <td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="12%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.0%;">
  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">-1.3</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="2%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="12%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.0%;">
  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">-1.9</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>

</table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues
increased $3.1 million, or 3.1%, to $103.8 million in 2005 from $100.7 million
in 2004.&#160; Revenue increases were realized
in Private Wealth Management, Institutional Investment Management, Mercantile
Funds, and Brokerage.&#160; Revenues declined
in Private Banking despite strong loan and deposit growth.&#160; Growth in IWM revenues was principally due to
stronger equity and real estate markets during 2005 compared with 2004,
increased new sales in Private Wealth Management and increased brokerage
activity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Private Wealth Management benefited from a modest improvement in the
equity markets, 19% growth in annualized revenues from new sales compared with
the prior year and the addition of new assets at higher fees than the
prevailing average.&#160; These trends were
partially offset by a decline in income-related fees associated with the
current low interest rate environment.&#160;
The increase in revenues partially reflects a $0.3 billion, or 2.1%,
increase in Personal Assets Under Administration to $12.5 billion.&#160; Personal Assets with Investment
Responsibility increased $0.1 billion, or 1.5%, to $8.7 billion, while Assets
with No Investment Responsibility increased $0.2 billion, or 4.5%,
to&nbsp;$3.8&nbsp;billion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Institutional Investment Management benefited from an increase in real
estate pension fees.&#160; This was partially
offset by a decline in the revenues of our Boyd Watterson Asset Management (&#147;Boyd
Watterson&#148;) subsidiary and the loss of one significant account in the custody
area.&#160; The decline in revenues at Boyd
Watterson is primarily attributable to a decline in equity assets under
management and the spin-off of one part of its business.&#160; Total Institutional Assets Under Administration
(including Boyd Watterson) declined $1.6&nbsp;billion, or 4.5%, to $33.7
billion.&#160; Institutional Assets with
Investment Responsibility declined $0.6 billion, or 4.9%, to
$11.6&nbsp;billion.&#160; Assets Under
Administration with No Investment Responsibility declined $1.0 billion, or
4.3%, to $22.1 billion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Mercantile Funds benefited from higher assets flows into the funds
and improved equity markets.&#160; Mercantile
Fund assets increased $0.1 billion, or 3.2%, to $3.9 billion, driven by an
11.0% increase in personal trust assets.&#160;
Brokerage commissions and income benefited from growth in the number of
accounts and assets held in accounts.&#160;
Brokerage assets increased 14.0% to $1.0 billion.&#160; In the table below, Mutual Fund assets and
Brokerage assets have been allocated to Personal and Institutional.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">47.8</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="2%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:2.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border:none;border-bottom:double windowtext 1.5pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.52%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">$</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="10%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;border-bottom:double windowtext 1.5pt;border-left:none;border-right:none;border-top:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:10.48%;">
  <p align="right" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">46.0</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" bgcolor="#CCEEFF" style="background:#CCEEFF;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.0%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2005, Assets Under Administration by IWM were
$46.5 billion, a decrease of $1.3 billion, or 2.7%, from the prior year.&#160; Bankshares had investment responsibility for
$20.6 billion, down $0.5 billion, or 2.4%, compared with the prior year. Additional
revenue growth will depend on continued new sales and increased distribution,
equity and bond market conditions and acquisitions, if any.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2005, expenses increased 4.8%, or $3.3 million, to $72.9 million,
compared with $69.6 million in 2004. Increases in personnel-related, technology
and occupancy expenses were offset by decreases in professional services,
travel and marketing expenses.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net interest income represents the largest source of Bankshares&#146;
revenue.&#160; Changes in both the level of
interest rates and the amount and composition of interest-earning assets and
interest-bearing liabilities affect it.&#160;
Interest rate risk represents one of the more significant risks facing
financial institutions like Bankshares.&#160;
See additional discussion under the caption &#147;Interest Rate Risk&#148; in section&nbsp;&#148;III.
ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION.&#148;&#160; It is
measured in terms of the effect changes in market interest rates have on net
interest income.&#160; Bankshares is slightly
asset sensitive, with assets repricing more quickly than liabilities in
response to changes in interest rates.&#160;
In a rising rate environment, Bankshares&#146; net interest margin (net
interest income expressed as a percent of average earning assets) expands,
causing the growth in net interest income to accelerate.&#160; Net interest income, on a fully
tax-equivalent basis, was $624.0 million for 2005.&#160; This represents an increase of 12.9%, or
$71.4 million, over the prior year&#146;s $552.5 million.&#160; In 2004, fully tax-equivalent net interest
income increased by $73.4 million, or 15.3%, over 2003.&#160; As previously noted, net interest income is
affected by changes in the volume of earning assets and the net interest margin
earned thereon.&#160; The &#147;Rate/Volume
Analysis&#148; table presents further details supporting this discussion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Average earning assets increased by $1.3 billion, or 10.5%, in 2005,
due in part to the CBNV acquisition.&#160;
Average total loans grew $1.3 billion, or 13.5%, during 2005, of which
the CBNV acquisition contributed approximately 32.1%, compared with an increase
of $1.6 billion, or 14.7% in 2004, which included a full year of the Farmers
acquisition.&#160; Average securities, the
other major component of earning assets, increased by $33.0 million, or 1.1%,
in 2005 compared with an increase of $204.6 million, or 7.4%, in the prior
year.&#160; The slowing growth of the
investment portfolio in 2005 is attributable to liquidity used to fund additional
loan growth.&#160; See the following section&nbsp;&#148;III.
ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION&#148; for a more in-depth discussion of balance
sheet trends.&#160; The overall growth in
average earning assets added $60.4 million to net interest income in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Also contributing to the increase in net interest income was a 9 basis
point increase in the net interest margin from 4.35% in 2004 to 4.44% in 2005,
compared with a 3 basis-point increase from 4.32% in 2003.&#160; The increase was attributable to a 20 basis
point increase in the benefit derived from noninterest-bearing sources of
funds, which was partially offset by an 11 basis point decline in the spread
between the yield on earning assets and the cost of interest-bearing
liabilities.&#160; The benefit from
noninterest-bearing funds increased due primarily to a $343.8 million increase
in net noninterest-bearing funds and the rising rate environment.&#160; The decline in the net interest spread
resulted from intensified competitive pressure on deposit pricing and the
flatness of the yield curve, which caused the overall yield on the investment
portfolio to lag the increase in funding costs. The net improvement in the net
interest margin of 9 basis points added $11.0 million to net interest income in
2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During 2005, the Federal Reserve Board raised rates eight times, for a
total increase of 200 basis points, and the yield curve flattened
dramatically.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2004,
the spread between the 10-year and two-year Treasury note rates was 115 basis
points, and by December&nbsp;31, 2005, the spread had inverted to a negative 2
basis points.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Looking forward to 2006, management anticipates a moderate increase in
short-term interest rates in the near term. Given the current rate environment,
the shape of the yield curve and the competitive dynamic, it is difficult to
predict how these pressures will affect the net interest margin.&#160; Management feels that Bankshares&#146; balance
sheet is relatively well positioned with respect to Federal Reserve Board
interest rate changes; however, competition for customers is expected to remain
intense.&#160; As Bankshares expands in new
markets, it is possible that spreads and margins may compress due to loan and
deposit pricing competition and the effort to achieve sensible growth from
small existing market positions. &#160;For
additional information regarding interest rate sensitivity, see the discussion
under &#147;Interest Rate Risk&#148; in &#147;III. ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION.&#148;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">SOURCES OF
  INCOME</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="12%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:12.5%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.94%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
  </td>
  <td width="36%" valign="bottom" style="border:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:36.82%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">USES OF
  INCOME</font></p>

million for both 2004 and 2003 are included in the calculation of commercial
real estate loan rate variances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)&nbsp;Tax-equivalent adjustments of $1.0 million for 2005, $0.9
million for 2004 and $1.3 million for 2003 are included in the calculation of
construction loan rate variances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)&nbsp;Tax-equivalent adjustments of $2.1 million for 2005, $2.2
million for 2004 and $1.9 million for 2003 are included in the calculation of
investment securities rate variances.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(5)&nbsp;Changes attributable to mix (rate and volume) are included in
the volume variance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Interest Income</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fully tax-equivalent interest income amounted to $822.9 million in
2005, an increase of $157.1 million, or 19.1%, from $665.8 million in 2004.&#160; This compares favorably with the $69.4
million, or 11.6%, increase in 2004 from 2003.&#160;
The increase in 2005 was due to growth in average loans and securities
that contributed $85.9 million, and an increase in market interest rates,
resulting in a $71.2 million increase from the higher yield on earning
assets.&#160; During 2004, the $99.1 million
in additional interest income from growth in average loans and securities was
offset by a decline in market interest rates, resulting in a $29.7 million
reduction in interest income from lower earning assets.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At year-end 2005, the prime rate was 7.25%, compared with 5.25% and
4.00% at year-end 2004 and 2003, respectively.&#160;
The average prime rate was 6.19% for 2005, compared with 4.35% for 2004,
an increase of 184 basis points.&#160; The
yield on average total loans in 2005 was 6.40%, a 73 basis-point increase from
5.67% in 2004.&#160; The commercial,
construction and home equity loan portfolios are the most sensitive to changes
in short-term interest rates.&#160; The
average yield on the construction and home equity loan portfolios increased 150
basis points and 156 basis points, respectively, while the commercial loan
portfolio yield increased 110 basis points over 2004.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">32</font></p>

<div style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><hr size="2" width="100%" noshade color="gray" align="left"></div>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The commercial real estate loan portfolio includes both fixed and
variable-rate loans and the average portfolio yield increased 64 basis
points.&#160; The residential real estate and
consumer loan portfolios are affected mostly by intermediate and long-term
rates and do not move with the prime rate.&#160;
The yields on the consumer loan portfolio and the residential real
estate portfolios decreased by 38 basis points and 2 basis points,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The yield on investment securities, 3.85% in 2005, increased 2 basis
points, from 3.83% in 2004.&#160; The yield on
the portfolio decreased 36 basis points in 2004 from 4.19% in 2003.&#160; Bankshares has been changing the mix of the
portfolio to offset the negative impact on interest income from reinvesting at
lower yields.&#160; During 2005 Bankshares
continued to follow a strategy to diversify the portfolio to a mix of U.S.
Treasury, U.S. Government agencies and mortgage-backed securities.&#160; This has resulted in a mix of 17.0%, 31.0%
and 47.0% of treasury, agency and mortgage-backed securities, respectively, in
2005.&#160; The other 5.0% of the investment
securities was comprised of 3.0% municipals and 2.0% other investments at
year-end.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Interest Expense</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Total interest expense in 2005 was $198.9 million, an increase of $85.7
million, or 75.6%, from $113.3 million in 2004.&#160;
The increase in interest expense for 2005 was attributable to an
increase in the rate paid on total interest-bearing funds of 73 basis points
and a 10.9% growth in average balances.&#160;
Total interest expense in 2004 was $4.0 million less than the $117.2
million reported in 2003.&#160; With the
expectation that the Federal Reserve Board will increase short-term rates again
in 2006, management anticipates that rates paid on managed-rate deposits (savings,
checking plus interest and money market accounts) will increase.&#160; See the discussion under &#147;Interest Rate Risk&#148;
in &#147;III. ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION&#148; for further information regarding
Bankshares&#146; exposure to changes in interest rates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The rate paid on average total interest-bearing deposits was 1.70% in
2005, an increase of 59 basis points from 1.11% for the prior year.&#160; The rate paid on savings, checking plus
interest and money market accounts increased 10 basis points, 2 basis points
and 78 basis points, respectively.&#160;
Certificates of deposit of $100,000 and over increased 119 basis points,
while the rate paid on other time deposits increased 52 basis points in 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The most interest rate sensitive source of funds is short-term
borrowings.&#160; This category is comprised
of federal funds purchased, securities sold under agreements to repurchase and
commercial paper.&#160; The duration of these
funds is very short, with most repricing daily. Reflecting the rate
environment, the rate paid on short-term borrowings increased 153 basis points
to 2.37% in 2005, after having increased by 18 basis points in 2004 to
0.84%.&#160; The rate paid on long-term debt
increased 96 basis points in 2005, following a decline of 16 basis points in
the prior year.&#160; The increase is related
primarily to the increase in interest rate swap costs on Bankshares&#146; long-term
debt.&#160; The $200.0 million of 10-year debt
issued by MSD&amp;T in the fourth quarter of 2001, issued at a fixed rate of
5.70%, were converted to a floating rate through an interest rate swap.&#160; The notes reprice quarterly and carried an
effective cost of 4.24% during 2005 versus 2.38% in 2004.&#160; Additionally, Bankshares issued $300.0
million of subordinated debt in April&nbsp;2003.&#160; The notes were issued at a fixed rate of
4.63%.&#160; Subsequently, $150.0 million of
this debt was converted to a floating rate through interest rate swaps.&#160; The effect of the swaps lowered the cost on
the $300.0 million debt to 4.37% during 2005 versus 3.46% in 2004.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">33</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h5 style="font-weight:bold;margin:0in 0in .0001pt;page-break-after:auto;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest Income</font></b></h5>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest income for 2005 increased by $29.2 million, or 13.6%, to
$243.1 million compared with $213.9 million for 2004.&#160; The table above shows the major components of
noninterest income.&#160; IWM revenue includes
personal and institutional fee income related primarily to trust, brokerage and
custody services.&#160; IWM revenue
represented the largest source of noninterest income at 39.4%.&#160; Revenues increased 6.3% to $95.8 million in
2005.&#160; Growth in IWM revenue was due
principally to stronger equity markets during 2005 compared with 2004,
increased new sales in Private Wealth Management and increased brokerage
activity.&#160; Additional growth will depend
on continued new sales and increased distribution, equity and bond market
conditions and further acquisitions, if any.&#160;
See the preceding discussion in &#147;Segment Reporting&#148; for additional
information relating to IWM.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Service charges on deposit accounts decreased slightly from 2004.&#160; The decrease was related primarily to
increased earnings credits used to calculate service charges to our business
customers, which resulted from the rising interest rate environment.&#160; Overdraft fees increased $1.9 million over
2004, partially offsetting the decline in service charges from our business
customers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Mortgage banking
fees increased $3.5 million, or 30.7%, over 2004 due to strong performance in
the commercial sector.&#160; Bankshares&#146;
mortgage banking-related revenue is comprised of loan origination fees, which
is the largest category, at 65.0%, of total mortgage banking fees; servicing
fees; originated mortgage servicing; and net gain on sales of mortgage
loans.&#160; Commercial mortgage
banking-related fees increased $3.5 million due to higher origination fees of
$2.3 million and increased income of $1.1 million from originated mortgage
servicing.&#160; Commercial servicing income
was nearly flat compared with the prior year.&#160;
Commercial mortgages are brokered to an investor base with servicing
retained. &#160;Residential mortgage banking
fees for 2005 were nearly flat compared with 2004.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Investment
securities gains in 2005 mostly represent the restructuring of the securities
portfolio acquired from CBNV.&#160; The gains in
2004 represent sales of equity securities, with the balance related to the
continued restructuring of the investment securities held in the
available-for-sale portfolios.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nonmarketable investment income represents revenues derived from
investing in private equities, hedge funds-of-funds (&#147;hedge funds&#148;), Federal
Reserve Banks and Federal Home Loan Bank securities acquired to meet various
regulatory requirements and bank-owned life insurance (&#147;BOLI&#148;).&#160; In 2005, nonmarketable investment income
increased $8.5 million, or 74.1%, over 2004 as a result of better private
equity investment performance and higher income from bank-owned life insurance
(&#147;BOLI&#148;).&#160; These increases were partially
offset by a decline in hedge fund income.&#160;
The increase in BOLI revenue was due to better performance and the
purchase of an additional $50.0 million in the third quarter of 2005, bringing
total investments in BOLI to $152.6 million.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">34</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other income includes several categories.&#160; Electronic banking fees consist of merchant
card processing fees, foreign ATM fees and check card fees.&#160; These fees increased by $2.2 million, or
10.1%, from 2004 due to higher volumes.&#160;
Charges and fees on loans consist of letters of credit fees, late fees
and other assessed loan fees and increased $1.8 million, primarily due to
higher letters of credit fees.&#160; Insurance
revenues increased $1.7 million and are derived from fee income related to the
sale and servicing of insurance products.&#160;
All other income increased $7.0
million over 2004 due primarily to a $2.7 million increase in gains on sales of
bank-owned premises and $3.3 million in higher capital markets-related revenue.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Noninterest Expenses</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noninterest expenses increased $28.9 million, or 7.4%, from 2004.&#160; The table above shows the major components of
noninterest expenses.&#160; The principal
reasons for the year-over-year increase were expenses of approximately $8.0
million related to the acquisition of CBNV; higher incentive compensation
related to improved operating performance; base compensation and staffing
increases; higher occupancy expense due to the December&nbsp;2004 sale of
Bankshares&#146; headquarters building and the outsourcing of IWM back-office functions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Controlling costs and maintaining operational efficiencies remains a
primary objective for Bankshares.&#160; A
closely monitored key measure is Bankshares&#146; overall efficiency ratio.&#160; It is computed by dividing noninterest
expenses by the sum of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis and
noninterest income.&#160; Bankshares&#146;
efficiency ratio was 48.53% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005 compared
with 51.14% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; The cash operating efficiency ratio excludes
amortization expense for intangibles and nonoperating income and expenses, such
as securities gains and losses and other significant gains, losses or expenses
(such as those associated with integrating acquired entities&#146; operations into
Bankshares) unrelated to Bankshares&#146; core operations.&#160; When calculating certain performance ratios,
Bankshares believes that excluding these costs and income helps the investor to
evaluate and compare the results of our core, ongoing business operations.&#160; Bankshares&#146; cash operating efficiency ratio
was 47.61% and 49.63% for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2005 and 2004,
respectively.&#160; See &#147;Reconciliation of
Non-GAAP Measures&#148; found in Item 7. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Salaries, which include base compensation, commissions, incentive
compensation and stock-based compensation, are the largest component of
noninterest expense at 47.6%.&#160; Salaries
increased $12.6 million, or 6.7%.&#160; Nearly
one-quarter of this increase, ($3.0 million) was due to the CBNV
acquisition.&#160; Also contributing to the
increase were higher incentive compensation expenses of $8.3 million related to
improved operating performance and $6.3 million in merit and staffing
increases.&#160; Stock-based compensation was
nearly flat when compared with 2004.&#160;
Partially offsetting these increases was a reduction in salaries expense
by $2.5 million based on the deferral of loan origination costs.&#160; Employee benefit expenses increased nearly
$1.5 million, or 3.4%.&#160; This increase was
due primarily to higher payroll taxes and pension expense.&#160; Partially offsetting this increase was a $1.3
million rebate from a medical insurance provider due to good claims experience.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">35</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Net occupancy expense, which includes premises depreciation, rents,
maintenance and utilities, increased due to an increase of approximately $5.0
million related to the loss of outside tenant income due to the sale of
Bankshares&#146; headquarters building in December&nbsp;2004.&#160; The net addition of 14 new branches,
primarily from the CBNV acquisition, also contributed to the increase.&#160; Furniture and equipment expenses include
depreciation, rental and maintenance expense associated with the upkeep and
improvement of hardware and computer software.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other expenses
consist of professional services, advertising and promotion, electronic
banking, intangible amortization, outsourcing and all other expenses.&#160; Other expenses increased $10.8 million, or
12.4%, in 2005.&#160; The CBNV acquisition
contributed $2.4 million to this increase.&#160;
Professional fees decreased $3.4 million in 2005 due primarily to a $1.4
million reduction in fees related to the implementation of compliance measures
under The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 and a decrease of $1.5 million related to
a litigation matter in 2004.&#160; The
increase in electronic banking expense of $2.4 million in 2005 was driven by
volume increases.&#160; This increase was not
completely offset by increased revenue generated from these services (referred
to in the Noninterest Income section).&#160;&#160;
Amortization of other identifiable intangibles increased to $8.8 million
in 2005, from $8.1 million in 2004, as a direct result of the CBNV
acquisition.&#160; The remaining increase in
other expenses over 2004 was due primarily to $5.9 million in higher fees
related to the outsourcing of IWM back-office functions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">III. ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Investment Securities</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares&#146; investment securities portfolio is structured to manage
liquidity, interest rate risk and regulatory capital and to take advantage of
market conditions that create more economically attractive returns on
investments.&#160; At December&nbsp;31, 2005,
the total investment securities portfolio was $3.1 billion compared with $2.9
billion at December&nbsp;31, 2004, with net unrealized losses of $52.2 million
and $3.2 million for the same periods.&#160;
The portfolio consists of short-term and intermediate-term U.S. Treasury
and U.S. Government agency obligations, adjustable-rate mortgage-backed
securities (ARMs) and intermediate average-life agency collateralized mortgage
obligations (CMOs).&#160; More than 99.5% of
the total investment portfolio is classified as available-for-sale.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At year-end 2005, the weighted-average maturity of the debt securities
available-for-sale portfolio was 2.3 years compared with 2.4 years at year-end
2004.&#160; Since 50.0% of this portfolio was
mortgage-backed securities, the expected remaining maturity may differ from
contractual maturity because borrowers may have the right to prepay obligations
before the underlying mortgages mature.&#160;
The fair value of the bond securities available-for-sale portfolio at December&nbsp;31,
2005 was 98.2% of amortized cost, compared with 99.8% at December&nbsp;31,
2004.&#160; The fair value and unrealized loss
on securities as of December&nbsp;31, 2005, segregated by those securities that
have been in an unrealized loss position for a year or more, was $2.0 billion
and $22.0 million, respectively.&#160; Because
the declines in fair value were due to changes in interest rates, not in
estimated cash flows or credit quality, no charge from an other-than-temporary
impairment was recorded at December&nbsp;31, 2005.&#160; The reference point for determining those
securities in an unrealized loss position is quarter-end.&#160; As such, it is possible that a security had a
market value that exceeded its amortized cost on other days during the past 12-month
period.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The estimated effects of a 200 basis point increase or decrease in
interest rates on the fair value and the expected remaining maturity of the
mortgage-backed securities available-for-sale portfolio are provided in the
table below.</font></p>

<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Loan Portfolio</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A comparative chart of average loan balances is included below;
year-end balances are in Note No.&nbsp;4 (Loans and Allowance for Loan Losses)
of the Financial Statements.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Loans totaled $11.6 billion for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005,
an increase of 13.5% over the $10.2 billion for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2004.&#160; Loans averaged $11.0 billion in
2005 compared with $9.7 billion in 2004, an increase of 13.5%.&#160; On average in 2005, commercial loans grew
6.4%; commercial real estate grew 17.7%; construction grew 28.8%; residential
real estate loans grew 7.2%; home equity lines grew 12.6%; and consumer loans
increased 13.7% over 2004.&#160; The increases
in the various loan categories resulted from both organic growth and the CBNV
acquisition.&#160; On an average basis, the
percentage of commercial real estate loans to total loans increased to 31.2% in
2005 from 30.0% in 2004.&#160; Additionally,
construction loans increased in 2005 from 2004, while commercial loans declined
to 26.3% in 2005 from 28.1% in 2004.&#160;
Strong demand continued throughout 2005 for real estate-based loans
including commercial, residential and home equity loans and lines.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Deposits</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares&#146; primary source of funding for its investing and lending
activities is deposits gathered by the 240 branches of its banking
affiliates.&#160; Average total deposits in
2005 were $11.4 billion, representing an increase of $1.0 billion, or 9.6%,
over the prior year average of $10.4 billion.&#160;
The CBNV acquisition accounted for a substantial portion of this growth,
contributing 61.5% based on $626.9 million in acquired deposits.&#160; For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005,
81.1% of the funding for average earning assets was derived from deposits,
compared with 81.8% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2004.&#160; The affiliate-banking model positions
Bankshares to compete not only with the large national and regional banking
companies in the gathering of these funds, but also with local community
banks.&#160; Based on historical experience,
management believes Bankshares is positioned to retain this core customer base,
although pricing pressure is expected to be intense.&#160; Bankshares continues to promote its cash
management services to its commercial customers in order to maintain and expand
this key source of funding.&#160; However,
should there be an outflow of deposits, a reversal of recent trends, the
investment portfolio should provide adequate liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In 2005, interest-bearing deposits represented 72.3% of average total
deposits and were $8.2 billion, reflecting growth of 9.5% from 2004.&#160; Growth in savings accounts slowed as customers
demonstrated a stronger preference for higher yielding money market and
certificates of deposit accounts.&#160;
Checking plus interest accounts increased 8.5% from 2004 to $1.4
billion.&#160; Certificates of deposit
$100,000 and over and other time deposits increased 16.0% on average in 2005
over 2004 with the CBNV acquisition contributing approximately 51.5% of the
growth.&#160; Total average
noninterest-bearing deposits rose from $2.9 billion in 2004 to $3.2 billion in
2005, or 9.9%, and represented 27.7% of average deposits.&#160; Demand for this product has been strong among
both commercial and retail customers throughout 2005.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<div>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Risk Management</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares has
established an integrated risk management structure in which senior management
regularly identifies, measures and manages risks.&#160; The Chief Risk Officer coordinates and
directs the work of several standing management committees charged with
managing the risks Bankshares faces and provides regular reports to the Audit
Committee.&#160; These committees are listed
below.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;text-indent:0in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Credit Quality Committee</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Credit Quality Committee oversees the establishment of consistent
credit quality policies and, among other responsibilities, works with
management in determining important financial reporting information, including
the allowance for loan and lease loss reserve.&#160;
A centralized loan review function is charged with analyzing the risks
and quality of the lending portfolios.&#160;
Among other things, Loan Review reaffirms or modifies individual
loan-risk ratings in accordance with Bankshares&#146; Loan Policy.&#160; The Committee reports quarterly to the Audit
Committee.&#160; The members of the Committee
include the senior vice presidents of Loan Review, the Chief Financial Officer,
Chief Administrative/Risk Officer, Vice Chairman/Chief Operating Officer and
Chief Executive Officer of Bankshares, the senior vice president of Credit
Policy at MSD&amp;T, the executive vice president of Affiliate Administration
and the Bankshares&#146; Treasurer.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Asset and Liability Committee </font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Asset and Liability Committee (&#147;ALCO&#148;) manages interest rate risk,
market risk and liquidity risk.&#160; These
risks are described in more detail elsewhere in this document. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Compliance Committee</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Compliance Committee establishes compliance guidelines and ensures
strict compliance with all relevant regulatory and statutory requirements for
Bankshares and its affiliates.&#160; In
creating the Compliance Committee, management intended to foster a strong
compliance function, which would establish global compliance guidelines and
ensure strict compliance for Bankshares and its affiliates with relevant
banking statutes and regulations, including the Bank Secrecy Act, anti-money
laundering statutes and fair lending statutes.&#160;
A chief compliance officer oversees compliance with existing regulatory
requirements and is responsible for developing a comprehensive training
program.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Compliance deficiencies are reported to senior management through the
General Counsel and the Compliance Committee.&#160;
As part of its mission, the Committee regularly assesses Bankshares&#146;
compliance efforts and maintains a high level of awareness about compliance and
its effect on daily activities.&#160; The
chief compliance officer prepares a report, at least quarterly, that includes</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)&nbsp;the results of compliance monitoring activities and any
compliance concerns identified with recommended corrective action,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)&nbsp;regulatory developments related to new and revised regulations
and proposed regulations, (3)&nbsp;compliance training activities,</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)&nbsp;compliance initiatives, (5)&nbsp;regulatory exams, and (6)&nbsp;customer
complaints.&#160; The Committee&#146;s meetings are
chaired by the General Counsel and are held quarterly.&#160; In addition, the chief compliance officer
presents the compliance report to the Audit Committee quarterly.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Disclosure Committee</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Disclosure Committee is comprised of senior representatives of all
of Bankshares&#146; business lines and is responsible for reviewing Bankshares&#146;
periodic filings and disclosures in order to ensure compliance with the
requirements of U.S. securities laws.&#160; In
conjunction with the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer,
the Disclosure Committee is charged with the design and oversight of internal
controls over financial reporting.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee conducts a systematic analysis of Bankshares&#146; annual and
quarterly filings and reports filed on Form&nbsp;8-K.&#160; It has established and evaluates the
disclosure policies and procedures relating to the various certification
requirements of the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, as
required by sections 302, 404, and 906 of The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002.&#160; The Committee, at least annually, performs a
formal risk assessment of the primary business processes/cycles that support
financial reporting.&#160; The Committee
reviews important changes in the law related to disclosure requirements with
Bankshares&#146; external and internal legal counsel.&#160; The Chief Financial Officer and his
subordinates monitor important changes in accounting standards and evaluate
changes in the organization that may affect internal controls over financial
reporting or that may require disclosure, and regularly report to the Committee
on such developments.&#160; The Committee
regularly reports to the Audit Committee.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Technology and Operations Committee</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Technology and Operations Committee evaluates operational risk on
an ongoing basis.&#160; The Committee has
developed an Operational and IT Risk framework, including the evaluation of key
risk indicators and the integration with existing Bankshares internal control
and risk-assessment efforts.&#160; Specifically,
the Committee ensures that risk management is a responsibility of all layers of
management, and it monitors the implementation of the various operational and
information technology risk policies of Bankshares.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Committee ensures that a structure and process exist for the
continuous identification and evaluation, and subsequent remediation, of
operational risk.&#160; Membership includes
eight individuals from the Operations&nbsp;&amp; Technology Division.&#160; Ad hoc members include representatives from
executive management, business units, Internal Audit, Financial Services and
Compliance.&#160;&#160; The President of MSD&amp;T
and the Chief Risk Officer/Chief Administrative Officer are kept apprised of
the Committee&#146;s activities.&#160; The Chair of
the Committee, the executive vice president of Operations&nbsp;&amp; Technology
Services, reports to the Audit Committee at least annually<b><font style="font-weight:bold;">.</font></b></font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">39</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Credit Risk Analysis</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares&#146; loans and commitments are substantially to borrowers
located in its immediate region.&#160;
Bankshares has restricted its participation in multibank credits where
Bankshares is not the managing or agent bank.&#160;
Central to the operation of a sound and successful financial institution
is the balanced management of asset growth and credit quality.&#160; Responsibility for loan underwriting and
monitoring is clearly fixed on key management personnel in each of our
affiliates and, ultimately, on the board of directors of each affiliate.&#160; These responsibilities are supported at the
holding company level by appropriate underwriting guidelines and effective
ongoing loan review.&#160; In addition,
Bankshares has set an internal limit for each affiliate bank that is well below
the regulatory limit on the maximum amount of credit that may be extended to a
single borrower.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares&#146; loan review function examines each affiliate bank at least
once every five quarters.&#160; These
examinations provide Bankshares&#146; management with an independent perspective as
to overall loan portfolio quality, risk profile, risk trends and credit
administration processes at each affiliate.&#160;
The Audit Committee receives quarterly reports on the findings.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ALLOWANCE AS A PERCENT OF PERIOD-END LOANS; NONPERFORMING LOANS AS A
PERCENT OF PERIOD-END LOANS</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">


<div>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Bankshares maintains an allowance for loan losses at a level considered
by management to be adequate to absorb potential losses inherent in the loan
portfolio.&#160; Each Bankshares affiliate is
required to maintain an allowance for loan losses adequate to absorb losses
inherent in the loan portfolio. Each affiliate&#146;s reserve is dedicated to that
affiliate only and is not available to absorb losses from another affiliate.
The allowance for loan losses is comprised of specific allocations to impaired
loans and general allocations to pools of loans not deemed impaired.&#160; It may also include an unallocated
amount.&#160; The portfolio review and the
calculation of the allowance for loan losses are performed on a quarterly basis
by Bankshares&#146; management.&#160; The
calculation is reviewed by the Bankshares Credit Quality Committee and each
affiliate bank as to its allowance.&#160; The
aggregate calculation establishes a targeted minimum level for the allowance at
each affiliate, subject to review and input from each affiliate.&#160; Final approval rests with the Credit Quality
Committee.&#160; The final evaluation is
reviewed with the Bankshares Audit Committee.&#160;
All loan loss reserves are subject to annual bank regulatory
examinations and determinations as to their methodology and adequacy.&#160; Overall, the determinations of the allowance
for loan losses incorporate SFAS No.&nbsp;114, &#147;Accounting by Creditors for
Impairment of a Loan - an amendment of FASB Statements No.&nbsp;5 and 15,&#148; and SFAS No.&nbsp;118,
&#147;Accounting by Creditors for Impairment of a Loan - Income Recognition and
Disclosure.&#148;&#160; Also incorporated in
determination of the allowance is SFAS No.&nbsp;5, &#147;Accounting for Contingencies&#148;;
guidance contained in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#146;s SAB No.&nbsp;102,
&#147;Loan Loss Allowance Methodology and Documentation&#148;; and the Federal Financial
Institutions Examination Council&#146;s Policy Statement on Allowance for Loan and
Lease Losses Methodologies and Documentation for Banks and Savings
Institutions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">ALLOCATION OF ALLOWANCE FOR LOAN LOSSES</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following table presents the amount of allowance for loan losses
and the percentage distribution of loan amounts in each category, at the date
shown.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-autospace:none;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" width="100%" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100.0%;">
 <tr>
  <td width="11%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:11.12%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom" style="padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:1.88%;">
  <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>
  </td>
  <td width="85%" colspan="24" valign="bottom" style="border:none;border-bottom:solid windowtext 1.0pt;padding:0in 0in 0in 0in;width:85.66%;">
